jobs.description:
What to Expect

Tesla is seeking highly motivated engineering students who thrive in a fast-paced environment and want to apply electrical concepts to real world projects. Our team drives collaboration with many engineering groups - team players only. Tesla moves quickly, so being self-motivated and disciplined is critical. You must be passionate, but direction changes quickly, so you must also be resilient. As an intern you will work directly with full-time engineers to design, prototype, test and launch new parts and processes to improve our batteries. Our projects include advanced cooling systems, cell interfaces and high voltage distribution. Every day we push the boundaries of what is possible for energy storage in our vehicles, demanding extreme attention to details and the highest standard of performance, quality and manufacturability.

What You’ll Do

- Design new battery electrical components that improve product metrics (performance, cost, mass)
- Own basic testing and analysis; support advanced testing and analysis
- Develop various test setups and fixtures to validate battery components
- Create schematics and layouts for complex circuits and assemblies
- Root cause test failures and process/manufacturing issues
- Collaborate with other teams inside Tesla (manufacturing, testing, NPI, supply chain, etc.)
- Create sources of truth to reference important findings

What You’ll Bring

- Currently working towards a BS, MS, or advanced degree in a relevant engineering program such as Mechanical Engineering, Automotive Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechatronics, or related field
- Strong knowledge of engineering fundamentals, such as mechanics, fluid dynamics, heat transfer, material properties and basic electronics
- Demonstrated hands-on abilities (e.g. machine shop skills, technical hobbies/academic projects, etc.) - Experience with student Formula Vehicle, Solar Car, etc. is a plus
- Proficiency in CAD modeling. CATIA V5/V6 and 3DX experience is a plus
- Strong knowledge of tolerance analysis, applying GD&T, finite element analysis (FEA), and basic thermal models
- Detail-oriented personality with top-tier documentation and reporting skills
- Fluency in English, German is a plus

jobs.occupation: Senior Cost Estimator, EMEA Infrastructure Development - (m/w/d) (Projektleiter/in / Projektmanager/in)
jobs.description:
What to Expect

The EMEA Infrastructure Development team is seeking a Senior Cost Estimator to serve as the subject matter expert in construction cost estimating across Tesla's EMEA portfolio, including Service Centers, Retail Stores, Delivery Hubs, and Non-SSD sites (R&D, Training, Offices, etc.) You will drive the transition from decentralized regional estimating to a centralized EMEA-wide approach — defining the methodology, standards, templates, and governance for how projects are evaluated. You will deliver independent, reliable construction cost estimates at every project stage, giving project teams, designers, procurement, and leadership a trusted reference for go/no-go decisions.

What You’ll Do

- Develop cost estimates from Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) through detailed CapEx budgets, with accuracy appropriate to each project stage (AACE estimate classes as reference framework)
- Produce high-level estimates based on historic data to support go/no-go decisions against key cost metrics
- Analyze plans, Due diligence reports and interpret designs; perform dimensional quantity take-offs; identify scope implied but not explicitly shown in design documents
- Develop and manage a Basis of Estimate for each project — scope, execution strategy, precision level, assumptions, exclusions, risks, and critical information
- Lead value engineering at early design stages, providing cost-driven feedback and recommendations to designers
- Visit project sites as required to validate scope, site conditions, and constraints in support of estimation — working from assumptions and scope definition provided by the Project Manager, Real Estate team and design team
- Support the Procurement and PMs with contractor pricing validation and bid leveling to ensure we are receiving good value for spends
- Contribute to continuous improvement of estimating processes
- Maintain and update the cost database, ensuring pricing reflects current market conditions, inflation, transport costs, and regional differentiation
- Deliver accurate, independently validated estimates to support ATP and go/no-go decisions; review outputs against historic pricing and regional benchmarks
- Provide expert input to Procurement on sourcing and pricing for atypical works or high cost-variance items

What You’ll Bring

- Degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, or related field — or equivalent professional experience
- 5+ years as a senior specialist or SME in project cost estimating, preferably in retail, commercial, industrial, or multi-site infrastructure rollout environments
- Practical knowledge of construction means and methods across civil, structural, architectural, MEP disciplines with the ability to translate technical knowledge into accurate, defensible cost advice
- Solid understanding of CapEx cost estimating from ROM through detailed CapEx budgeting; proven experience with quantity take-offs and design document interpretation
- Experience maintaining or developing pricing databases or cost libraries at a portfolio or multi-country level
- Ability of identifying main risks especially during ROM which could significantly impact the costs in a later stage
- Analytical, detail-oriented, and self-motivated; proactive communicator in a fast-paced, multicultural environment
- Experience building, leading, or transitioning to a centralized estimating function — methodology, SOPs, and standardization frameworks
- Proven track record as the go-to cost expert for project teams, designers, and leadership; authoritative cost advice with confidence, independence, and sound professional judgement
- Availability to travel across EMEA as required (up to 50%)
- English required; additional European language skills a strong plus

Nova (NASDAQ: NVMI) is a globally operating company and a leading provider of innovative metrology and process control solutions for semiconductor manufacturing.

With around 1,600 employees, 4 research and development centers, and 31 locations worldwide, we deliver valuable insights into the world’s most advanced industry. We leverage a variety of technological disciplines – including physics, optics, chemistry, and algorithms – to develop hardware and software solutions that measure virtually every modern computer chip in the world. Nova looks down to the atomic level, gains unique insights through dimensional, material, and chemical metrology, and provides customers with actionable data. This enables us to tackle critical challenges with differentiated solutions. Our exceptional, people-focused, and innovation-driven corporate culture ensures that every individual at Nova has the opportunity to make a real impact and push the boundaries of what is technologically possible.

We are looking for creative minds with high ambitions who see the seemingly impossible as a challenge and love to achieve innovative breakthroughs in a global, multidisciplinary team.

jobs.description:
The Leibniz Institute for Agricultural Engineering and Bioeconomy (ATB) is a pioneer and a driver of bioeconomy research. We create the scientific foundation to transform agricultural, food, industrial and energy systems into a sustainable bio-based circular economy. We develop and integrate techniques, processes and management strategies, effectively converging technologies to intelligently crosslink highly diverse bioeconomic production systems and to control them in a knowledge-based, adaptive and largely automated manner. We conduct research in dialogue with society, policymakers, industry and other stakeholders - knowledge-driven and application-inspired.

To support Economics of Technologies in Agriculture in the Technology Assessment Department we are seeking, at the earliest possible date a

Doctoral researcher (m/f/d) (75 %)

for the research area

„Economic analysis of innovative fenland use“

The economic analysis includes various lines of utilization of biomass from wet fenland sites and analysis of greenhouse gas abatement potentials resulting from the change in land use. Cost analysis includes approaches and cost estimates for planning, permission, management, and harvest of mixed vegetation, storage and transportation, and processing in innovative biomass utilization pathways. Labor times, costs, and potential savings from autonomous harvesting vehicles, among others, are identified. Reference uses and innovative business models are also considered to determine the economic viability of specific processes.

The aim of the project is to create a network of model and demonstration projects for the use of rewetted fens with representative fen areas, biomass utilization pathways and relevant actors in Brandenburg. Partners are in addition to ATB the Brandenburg State Office for the Environment (LfU), the University for Sustainable Development Eberswalde (HNEE), the Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research (ZALF) and the Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences (GFZ). The WetNetBB network is part of a network of model and demonstration projects (PaludiNet) coordinated by the Thünen Institute (TI) and Greifswald Moor Centrum (GMC) as PaludiCenter. The position is assigned to the Technology Assessment Department at the ATB, and close cooperation with the Systems Process Engineering Department is intended. 

Yourtasks

- Development of models for calculating the economic potential of different utilization systems on wet fenlands
- Recording and analysis of the labour time requirements of novel forms of use of wet fenlands
- Quantitative and qualitative evaluation of scientific results
- Development of scenario-based calculations of the costs of agricultural use through paludiculture on lowland bog sites
- Presentation of project results at scientific conferences and stakeholder meetings
- Writing of scientific publications and project reports

Your qualifications

- Very good university degree in agricultural economics or related subjects (Diploma or Master of Science)
- Knowledge and experience in economic analysis of agricultural systems
- Knowledge in statistical data analysis
- Strong interest in interdisciplinary collaboration
- Very good knowledge of written and spoken English
- Very good knowledge of German for communication with stakeholders and farmers
- Ability to work in a team and willingness to cooperate, reliability, flexibility, personal commitment and independent working skills
- EU driving license class B desirable

We offer

- Encouragement and support for PhD candidates in pursuing their doctoral studies in collaboration with partner universities
- An attractive, research-intensive, and interdisciplinary working environment
- A varied position at the interface of science and practice
- Excellent infrastructure for scientific work
- Access to national and international networks for your scientific development
- Training and further education opportunities
- Family-friendly working conditions to promote work-life balance
- Participation in the VBB company ticket or Deutschlandticket
- A workplace at the edge of a picturesque landscape, easily accessible by bike or public transport

The part-time position (30 hours/week) is initially limited to 4 years. Salary will be based on your qualifications and experience according to TV-L up to pay grade E 13.

For further information, please contact Dr. Andreas Meyer-Aurich (phone +49 331 5699-222) and visit our website at www.atb-potsdam.de (http://www.atb-potsdam.de) .

Have we piqued your interest? Then apply by 30 September 2026 with your cover letter, CV (without photo), and employment references and/or contact details of referees via our online application portal for this job posting (reference number 2026-TA-3) at www.atb-potsdam.de/en/career/vacancies (http://www.atb-potsdam.de/en/career/vacancies) . 

As a certified family-friendly institute, the ATB is committed to equal opportunities and diversity.
